metadata.title: The spatial and velocity distributions of hypervelocity stars

evidence.quote:
The unbound HVS, HE 0437-
5439, was proposed to be ejected out from the LMC
(Edelmann et al. 2005); and this object was excluded in
the original fits to the two disk planes in Lu et al. (2010).

Because of the short lifetime and long traveling
time of HE 0437-5439, it is suggested that this object
was originally a binary star when being ejected out from
the GC

notes: HE 0437-5439: Categorized as follow_up because the paper recalls its prior identification as an unbound HVS and analyzes its origin/disk-plane compatibility (T:p19-b1, T:p19-b31). The paper also gives aggregate samples of 16 unbound HVSs, 8 bound HVSs, and 4 HVS candidates (T:p2-b4; see also T:p2-b7), but does not provide individual names or source identifiers for those members, so they are not separately rostered.

HE 0437-5439: The paper mentions HE 0437-5439 only in the note added in proof (T:p19-b1 and T:p19-b31), discussing its proposed LMC origin, recent HST proper motion, and possible GC origin under the BBH mechanism. No numerical values for right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability are reported for this individual star.
